notes: Every place the plugin depends on the behavior of the claude, codex or grok CLI. /update-clis reads each release note against this list.
kind lane: what the external runner uses of the CLI. kind harness: what the plugin uses of Claude Code, Codex or Grok Build as the parent; a harness change never holds an update, it is reported.
coveredBy: the probe lanes of the same CLI that exercise the touchpoint (see PROBE_LANES in scripts/update-clis.ts). An empty list means no probe covers it: a contract change there holds the update.
measuredOn: the CLI version the behavior was measured on. pointers: file (from the plugin root) and an anchor text inside it; update-clis.test.ts fails when one goes missing.

touchpoints.contract: CLI 0.161.0 queue accepts messages for unloaded threads without starting them. A persisted thread loaded in the same local app-server consumes thread/queue/add after turn completion. Unix control sockets require WebSocket Upgrade. Client event IDs, queue/list and queue/delete support finite wake deduplication and cancellation; queued is not execution proof.

`codex exec --model <model> --config model_reasoning_effort="<effort>" --sandbox read-only|workspace-write --cd <dir> --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral --disable plugins --disable multi_agent --disable hooks --disable memories --json -` (prompt on stdin)

a same-provider `codex exec --ephemeral` receives no inherited Codex or Claude session identity, opens a fresh thread, and retains configuration and authentication; the parent still supplies the sandbox; default lanes disable recursive agents, explicit owners enable native delegation
`--json` stream: `thread.started` with `thread_id`, `item.completed` whose item is an `agent_message` with `text`, `turn.completed` with `usage`, `turn.failed` with `error.message`
`codex login status` exits 0 and prints "logged in"
the `--json` stream never reports the served model; the receipt pins it by argv (`reportedModel: null`, `modelEvidence: pinned-argv`)
`model_reasoning_effort` accepts every effort the sheets use for the codex families (low medium high xhigh max)

`codex sandbox -c sandbox_mode="workspace-write" -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -c sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=[...] -- <command>` runs the command under the seatbelt from its working directory: exports `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt`, lets it write the working directory and the writable roots, denies writes elsewhere. `-C` requires `--permission-profile` on 0.155.1, so the probe sets the working directory instead

`codex exec` runs the turn in its own process: it neither connects to the shared app-server daemon nor starts one, and `--ephemeral` writes no rollout under `~/.codex/sessions`. Only the TUI takes `--no-daemon`
`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` fields: name, version, skills path, interface (logo, displayName, descriptions, capabilities)
`agents/openai.yaml` with `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` keeps poteto-mode explicit-only
`codex plugin marketplace add <repo> --ref <tag>`, `codex plugin marketplace upgrade`, `codex plugin add pstack@pstack-vic`
`features.multi_agent` enables `spawn_agent` with `model` and `reasoning_effort` in a Codex parent

pointers.anchor: call `spawn_agent` with the descriptor's model and `reasoning_effort`

touchpoints.contract: `grok --sandbox read-only|workspace|none|off agent --always-approve --no-leader --agent-profile <private YAML-list profile> stdio`; bounded modes share the CLI sandbox mapping, including none inside an outer Codex sandbox; off requires explicit full-access. No global --tools or --no-subagents claim for ACP.

ACP agent-profile tools and disallowedTools are YAML lists. Profile input run_terminal_cmd becomes advertised run_terminal_command. Before one prompt and on catalog changes, available_commands_update._meta.tools must match the selected host builtins: four in read-only, five in write/full-access, plus search_tool/use_tool with MCP sources and web_search/web_fetch when requested. Configured-and-forwarded MCPs may expand the catalog with server__tool names; each segment starts with a letter or digit and contains only letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens. All names are recorded; duplicates, malformed names and unknown builtins fail. Host-only admits no MCP names. GROK_SUBAGENTS=0 and [subagents] enabled=false disable recursive agents; shell_environment_policy inherit=core remains staged. Receipts retain the generated profile SHA-256 and actual sandbox.

ACP protocolVersion 1 and clientType extension; authenticate cached_token; session/new; session/set_model with exact modelId and _meta.reasoningEffort; exactly one session/prompt. The measured skills-reload/workflows-reload status envelopes carry nested result objects and do not resolve pending requests or prove model use; unknown or duplicate reply IDs fail. Unsupported client requests get -32601 and perform no host operation.

Optional versioned T3 attachment binds urlEnv, bearerTokenEnv and previewTabId, requires explicit full-access and cannot be mixed with --capabilities. HTTP(S) loopback endpoint has no default port, userinfo, query or fragment. Authorization header is resolved only in memory; referenced variables are removed from child env; secrets and escaped values are redacted before output or evidence. Full access admits configured-and-forwarded Grok integrations and hooks.

session/update agent_message_chunk groups by streamStartMs. _x.ai/session_notification response_completed completes a generation. Tool activity invalidates narration. Terminal stopReason end_turn, nonempty final generation and _meta.usage.modelUsage prove the served model through shared modelFromUsage. CamelCase cumulative token fields normalize; unverified costUsdTicks stays null.

session/close gets one second of cleanup grace after accepted end_turn. Closed, RPC error or expired close grace are ACP receipt evidence. Close stdin, EOF grace, actual SIGTERM/SIGKILL and direct-child reap retain real exit status, including complete conversation with exit143. Cancellation and the absolute optional deadline remain authoritative through cleanup.

`grok --prompt-file <file> --model <model> --reasoning-effort <effort> --permission-mode <mode> --sandbox read-only|workspace|none --tools <list> --disallowed-tools <list> --output-format streaming-messages-json --cwd <dir> --no-subagents --disable-web-search --verbatim`
tool names `read_file`, `grep`, `list_dir`, `run_terminal_cmd`, and `search_replace` in isolated-write; `Agent`, `search_tool` and `use_tool` stay disallowed
a permission prompt cancels a headless turn in every mode; `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` never prompts
`streaming-messages-json`: an event `type: result` with `subtype`, `is_error`, `result`, `modelUsage`, `session_id`, `usage`, `total_cost_usd`

a valid `type: result` event whose `is_error` is `true` or whose `subtype` is not `success` is a failure; its message is `errors` (strings) joined, else `error`, `error.message` or `result`; `stop_reason` or `subtype` `cancelled` or `canceled`, or a message that starts with `User cancelled the execution` or `PermissionCancelled`, marks a provider cancellation (exit 130), and any other failure is `child-failed` (exit 70), also after exit 1. The headless guide of 1.0.46 documents `errors[]` on the error subtypes, `stop_reason` on `result`, `cancelled` among the turn stop reasons and exit 1 on error, and names the error subtypes `error_max_turns`, `error_during_execution` and `error_max_structured_output_retries`. The `api_error` subtype comes from the open's tests, and the `canceled` spelling and the two message prefixes from its parser (issue #78). The probe lanes pass only on `complete`, so none of them exercises this contract
the `modelUsage` key is the model with a build suffix (`grok-4.7-build`, `grok-4.6-build`); the matrix `reportedModel` patterns accept it

`grok models` exits 0 and prints "logged in" and the model id as a whole token, without an explicit authentication or model refusal; a requested-id refusal has one lexical subject, optionally quoted or bracketed, adjacent to its predicate; unrelated feature prose is not a model refusal; one retry after 5 s
`--reasoning-effort` accepts every effort the sheets use for the grok families (grok-4.7: low medium high xhigh)
inside Codex's seatbelt grok's own profile fails to initialise; the runner passes `--sandbox none` and the outer seatbelt governs
grok writes its session under `~/.grok`; under Codex's seatbelt that directory must be in `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots`

pointers.anchor: Grok also writes its session under `~/.grok`

touchpoints.contract: the `read-only` profile keeps grok's state and the system temporary directories writable

pointers.anchor: Grok's built-in read-only profile deliberately keeps its own state and system temporary directories writable

touchpoints.contract: on macOS the `read-only` and `workspace` profiles deny `openpty` (tmux cannot open a pane), crash Playwright's Chromium with SIGSEGV, and refuse `index.lock` under `.git/worktrees/<name>` (no commit in a linked worktree); the same argv with `--sandbox off` passes all three. `--model grok-build` is refused with `unknown model id`

pointers.anchor: cannot commit in a linked worktree

touchpoints.contract: a headless turn has no wall-clock limit of its own: grok ends it early only when the model's stream stalls (`models.inference_idle_timeout_secs`, 600 s by default), and a tool call that runs for minutes does not count as idle. The runner sets no limit unless `--timeout` is passed

pointers.anchor: The runner and its preflight have no implicit timeout.

touchpoints.contract: in headless, `run_terminal_cmd` keeps a command in the foreground and returns its output in the same turn; nothing moves it to the background after ~15 s. The model sets each call's timeout (it asked 180 s for a 150 s command) and grok caps it at 300 s (`toolset.bash.max_timeout_secs`): past the cap the command is killed (`timed_out: true`), not backgrounded, and the model retries it. The lane's tool list has no tool that waits on a background task

`GROK_CONFIG_PATH` names a TOML overlay merged above `config.toml` without replacing it; `shell_environment_policy.inherit = "core"` is on its allowlist and keeps a small platform set such as `PATH` and `HOME` in every sandbox mode; an inline `GROK_CONFIG` wins over the file. The shell grok opens for a tool command exports `GROK_AGENT`, which a machine's `~/.zshenv` uses to skip its credential exports

pointers.anchor: skip those exports when `GROK_AGENT` is set

touchpoints.contract: `claude -p --model <model> --effort <effort> --permission-mode plan|acceptEdits --setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --tools <list> --no-session-persistence --disable-slash-commands --disallowed-tools <list> --output-format json` (prompt on stdin)

An explicit owner keeps a fresh persisted session and --verbose root messages, and selects Agent, ListAgents, TaskStop and SendMessage through --tools and --allowedTools; TaskOutput was removed in 2.1.277 and a helper's result is its completion notification plus the files it wrote. Collect, continue and interrupt assigned local helpers through their native handles; launch success alone is insufficient. Native Agent isolation: worktree supplies a writer's own cwd and the completion notification names it. Untrusted project permissions.additionalDirectories is ignored in headless mode (stderr: this workspace has not been trusted); a sibling worktree is granted through the additionalDirectories task capability (--add-dir), which the owner's background helpers inherit. Ordinary lanes keep delegation and these lifecycle tools disabled.

pointers.anchor: Claude owners need the lifecycle tools

touchpoints.contract: `--output-format json`: an object, or a list of events whose last `type: result` carries the fields `result`, `is_error`, `modelUsage`, `session_id`, `usage`, `total_cost_usd`
`modelUsage` reports `claude-opus-5-5` for the opus family and `claude-fable-<n>` for the fable alias
`claude auth status --json` prints JSON with `loggedIn: true`

a nested `claude -p` starts as a fresh session once the parent's identity variables (`CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*`) are gone; `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is a credential, not identity, and outranks the keychain login (`auth status` reports `authMethod: oauth_token`)
`claude plugin validate --strict --json <path>` accepts the marketplace and the plugin manifest
SKILL.md frontmatter: `name`, `description`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`
agent frontmatter of the generated lanes: `model`, `effort`, `background: true`

`claude plugin marketplace add|update`, `claude plugin install|update|uninstall`, `claude --plugin-dir`; `claude plugin list --json` lists every install record (user, project, local) with its projectPath, and `claude plugin update --scope <scope>` moves the record of that scope for the cwd's project, except that from a linked worktree it resolves the local scope to the main checkout's local record when there is one (`updateOutcome: up_to_date` against that record, measured 2026-10-08), and to the worktree's own only without it; a session in a linked worktree loads the main checkout's local record, then its project record, and the worktree's own local record only without both, so a behind worktree-keyed local record next to a main-checkout record is inert (session init `plugins[].path`, desktop 2.1.293 and CLI 2.1.295); a session that starts in a linked worktree with no record keyed by it writes one when local settings enable the plugin, its own `.claude/settings.local.json` or the main checkout's, copying the version of an existing record; `claude plugin uninstall --scope <scope>` removes only the record keyed by the cwd but clears the plugin from the settings of the repository holding the cwd, which is the main checkout's `.claude/settings.local.json` from a linked worktree or from a plain folder inside a checkout, and only the cwd's own from a folder that is its own repository (measured 2026-10-09 against a copied config with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`); no option targets a record by path

a non-interactive `claude -p` owner whose turn ends with a live background native helper or a live background Bash command of its own stays open and is re-invoked when that work finishes, producing more than one `result` event in one invocation, and the runner keeps the last; after 10 minutes of idle waiting it stops whatever is still running, helpers and the main conversation's commands alike, prints `Background tasks still running 10m after the last turn (…); stopping them. Set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 to wait indefinitely.` on stderr, runs no further turn and exits 0 with the earlier reply, which the runner records as complete; the runner therefore gives every Claude child CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 unless the caller's environment sets the variable, and an owner launched that way with an 11-minute command left running was awaited and its second turn reached the receipt (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.295; the helper re-invocation first on 2.1.292). On an update, confirm that 0 still disables the ceiling and that the stderr line still names the variable. Keep the turn open until each notification arrives (`TaskOutput` was removed in 2.1.277); an interactive root is re-invoked by background Bash completions and Monitor events (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.293 in the desktop app)

pointers.anchor: Draining is the parent's job in every harness mode
Background tasks still running 10m after the last turn

touchpoints.contract: `--add-dir <dir>`, one flag per additionalDirectories entry (repeated flags accumulate), grants the file tools read and write access to a directory outside the cwd in a headless `claude -p` session regardless of workspace trust, and the session's background helpers inherit it; `permissions.additionalDirectories` in an untrusted project's .claude/settings.json is ignored with the stderr warning `this workspace has not been trusted`. Bash commands in the added directory still follow the permission mode: headless acceptEdits denies `git -C <dir> status` (`This command requires approval`) while `ls` passes. In isolated-write the runner adds one `--allowedTools` rule `Bash(git -C <dir> <subcommand> *)` per entry for status, diff, log, show, rev-parse, add and commit; the lane, the owner and its background helpers run those, while other subcommands, `cd <dir> && git`, git options before the subcommand and other commands stay denied, and a broad `Bash(git -C <dir> *)` would also run `git -C <dir> -c alias.x=!<cmd> x`. Plan mode runs read-only git there without a rule.

pointers.anchor: Additional directories must be absolute, existing directories

touchpoints.contract: Agent fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached. You can run N subagents at once. Do not retry. If the user wants more concurrent subagents, ask them to increase CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS.` once N subagents (default 20) are running in the session, and creates no handle; a completed or TaskStop-stopped helper frees its slot at once (the next spawn was admitted before the completion notification arrived); SendMessage resumes a completed or TaskStop-stopped helper even while N are running, the resumed helper counts as running, and spawns are rejected until the count drops below N; ListAgents states no limit (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.292 headless with N=2 and on the 2.1.293 desktop root with the default; the resume on 2.1.295 headless with N=2)

pointers.anchor: A resume is admitted past the limit
states that number only in its rejection text

touchpoints.contract: In a root inside the desktop app (CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=claude-desktop) a scheduled prompt (one-shot CronCreate, /loop, ScheduleWakeup) is delivered only at the first turn end with no background task alive, counting background shells and subagents, even a subagent ListAgents already lists as completed while its own shell runs; a terminal root (CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli) on the same binary delivers it on time with a background shell alive (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.293). This is why the desktop root's tick is not /loop 1h.

pointers.anchor: o `/loop 1h` não serve para o Tick

touchpoints.contract: The desktop root's tick is a Bash command with run_in_background true and a timeout above one hour (without one the host ends it at thirty minutes; the maximum is two hours): its exit opens a root turn with its output in the notification (9 to 12 s after the output in two short cycles; a background command's exit also woke a root with a background owner alive), and TaskStop ends it. It ends with its session: the session resumed under the same id with --resume gets one task-notification with status stopped (`Background shell command didn't finish before the previous session ended`) and never its completion, so a resumed root re-arms it (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.293, the resume in a terminal root on the app's binary; app sessions resumed on 2.1.275 and 2.1.284 got the same notification).

pointers.anchor: That root arms the tick as one `Bash` command
A resumed desktop root re-arms it.

touchpoints.contract: A background subagent keeps SendMessage, and SendMessage to `main` opens a new turn in the root that launched it; the root's SendMessage to the subagent's agent ID resumes an idle one in place (`Resuming agent`) and queues for a running one until its next tool round (`queued for delivery`). The two owners of one autopilot program sent every report this way (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.293 in a desktop root).

pointers.anchor: o Dono manda cada aviso por `SendMessage` para `main`

touchpoints.contract: A desktop root and its background owners have neither TodoWrite nor TaskCreate; ToolSearch for them answers `No matching deferred tools found`, so the Playbooks todolist lives in todo.md in the run's notes (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.293 in two desktop roots and two owners). TaskList, where present, lists todo items, not agents.

A native subagent's transcript is ~/.claude/projects/<encoded root cwd>/<root session id>/subagents/agent-<agent id>.jsonl with agent-<agent id>.meta.json beside it (agentType, worktreePath, worktreeBranch, description, spawnDepth); its records carry isSidechain true, its agentId, the root's sessionId and its own cwd. Its environment has the root's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and no agent id or root cwd, and nothing exists under ~/.claude/projects/<its own encoded cwd>/. The root's Agent result names the file as output_file through a symlink in the root's tasks directory (measured 2026-10-08 on 2.1.293 with a worktree-isolated background owner).

Grok root on T3 ACP stdio: spawn_subagent background/cwd/isolation/resume_from; run_terminal_command block_until_ms=0; get_command_or_subagent_output task_ids/timeout_ms; kill_command_or_subagent task_id; monitor emits root wake events.

Native Grok agents bind the exact model and effort from agent frontmatter. Plugin agent types are namespaced. Agent/Task deny recursive spawning on ordinary lanes. Owners need effective subagents.max_depth >= 2 and an observed owner → helper setup probe.

The root arms its hourly audit as a `monitor` running the plugin's ticker (persistent, ten-hour ceiling in 1.0.46, stopped through the retained handle). The detached scheduler and Grok's /loop run separate subagents and do not perform root audits.

pointers.anchor: Arm the hourly root audit with `monitor`

touchpoints.contract: Task capabilities keep the descriptor and sandbox while selecting native web, configured skills/plugins, named HTTP MCP sources or an owner. Codex owners enable multi_agent and keep a fresh persisted session; ordinary lanes remain ephemeral. CLI receipts record profile SHA-256 and requested capabilities; access requires an actual source call, not a listed catalog.

pointers.anchor: Task capabilities for local CLI sessions

touchpoints.contract: `codex exec --add-dir <DIR>`, one flag per additionalDirectories entry (repeated flags accumulate), adds a writable root beside the primary workspace under --sandbox workspace-write; a lane wrote through a shell redirect and ran git status in a sibling worktree of another repository.

Task capability profiles preserve the assigned descriptor, sandbox and fresh session. HTTP mcpSources name/url entries become session/new.mcpServers attachments; explicit source.tools are requested scope injected in the brief, not an enforced effective-catalog allowlist. Ambient configured sources remain trusted; listing a tool is no proof of access. Skills true uses accessible SKILL.md instructions through read_file on CLI or ACP; no native Skill tool is claimed. MCP sources require ACP, Grok owners always fail, and T3 attachment mixing fails before reservation. Receipts retain requested capabilities and source-file SHA-256 separately from the observed catalog.

An explicit web task adds web_search/web_fetch to the CLI tool list and omits --disable-web-search, retaining --no-subagents and the bounded sandbox. Grok 1.0.46 emits server_tool_use web_search, web_search_tool_result and server_tool_use.web_search_requests in the terminal usage.
